topic: Data flow diagrams: context diagram, level 0, balancing and rules
title: A level-0 DFD for the admissions office
instructions:
## Data in, data out

The admissions office receives **application forms** from **Applicants**, checks them against the **Programme requirements** store, records them in an **Applications** store, and sends each applicant an **admission decision**. The **Registry** receives a **list of admitted students**.

## Do this

Write the **level-0** DFD: two external entities, three processes (`P1 "Receive application"`, `P2 "Assess application"`, `P3 "Issue decision"`), two data stores, and **named** data flows. Every process needs an input and an output; stores and entities only connect to processes.

config.starter:
diagram: dfd
entity Applicant
entity Registry
process P1 "Receive application"

initialState.source:
diagram: dfd
entity Applicant
entity Registry
process P1 "Receive application"

hints: Applicant -> P1 : application form names the flow; P1 -> D1 : application record stores it.
P2 reads the requirements: D2 -> P2 : programme requirements, and the application: D1 -> P2 : application.
P3 -> Applicant : admission decision and P3 -> Registry : admitted students list.

checks.label: Applicant sends an application form to P1
Decision goes back to the Applicant
DFD rules: no miracles, black holes or store-to-store flows; all flows named

realityNote: Balancing means the inputs and outputs of the context diagram (one process, the whole system) match the external flows of level 0. Analysts still draw DFDs for data-heavy systems because they show what moves where before any class or screen exists.
